text.p: Telecoms shares fell on Wednesday after Telecom Italia's planned "supercordless" phone fell foul of Italy's antitrust authority.
Telecom Italia Mobile (TIM) fell 2.19 percent to 3,260 lire and was the third busiest stock on a quietly lower the Milan bourse after earlier falling to 3,240.
State-controlled holding company Stet was 1.39 percent lower at 5,450 and Telecom Italia itself fell 1.19 percent to 3,480.
A spokesman for the antitrust authority said the body would issue a formal opinion following statements by its president, Giuliano Amato, on Tuesday.
Amato said Telecom Italia's planned new venture was "a mobile phone to all intents and purposes".

The company said last week it was planning to launch a "supercordless" phone around Christmas that would boost the reception of ordinary domestic cordless phones, enabling users to take their home telephone out and about on long distances.

Telecom Italia managing director Francesco Chirichigno said the group was investing 1.8 billion lire in the venture, to be called "Fido", and said he did not expect it to compete with regular mobile phones.
But Amato disagreed, saying "Fido" could not be considered "a simple extension of fixed line (telephony)".

TIM, Europe's biggest phone operator, suffered a further blow when figures showed it was running virtually neck-and-neck with Omnitel, the consortium controlled by Olivetti, in enrolling new subscribers for their GSM phones.
Olivetti shares, which have yo-yoed in recent sessions on wide concerns about the group as a whole, were 3.46 percent firmer at 452 lire, having hit a new record low of 435 lire on Tuesday.
